title: How the Magnolia band played and hometown band members
summary: The brass band could jazz after learning music; Robinson lists men in the band at home.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Did he let them jazz it up once in a while by hand?
Well, yeah, see after they learned their music and they could play it any way they want. You understand? Play it the way they want. And they could play a lot of head numbers themselves, you see?
Do you remember any numbers they played?
Oh, I was a little too small then. I remember them playing. I was small then. But they had a good band.
Well, they had a band around their range too, huh?
Yeah, they had a band at my home. Now, I couldn't call all the person even that band. Let me see.
It was Chris from Magnolia or Derang? From Derang. He's from Derang.

Yeah. Now, I could tell you some of the persons in the band at home when I was a kid. Let me see. Walter Johnson, bass. Let me see. Alec Taylor, trumpet. Ben Cole, trumpet. Boyle Stevenson, trumpet. Boyle Stevenson, trumpet. Boyle Stevenson, trumpet. Weaver Jason, trumpet. William Stevenson, trumpet. Dan Sparks, alto. John Cole. Who was a solo alto. Joe Granson, baritone. I was a solo alto. He was a solo alto, Joe Granson, baritone, Robert Cooper.
